description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of difficulty levels across 1.4 million data entries in an open-source reasoning dataset, with five distinct categories: Medium, Hard, Easy, Very Hard, and Very Easy. The largest segment, colored light red, represents “Medium” difficulty, accounting for 51.8% of the dataset (725,892 entries). The second largest, in blue, corresponds to “Hard” at 25.7% (360,137 entries). The “Easy” category, shown in light green, comprises 11.2% (157,053 entries), followed by “Very Hard” in light orange at 6.5% (91,576 entries), and “Very Easy” in light purple at 4.7% (65,332 entries). A legend in the upper left corner matches each difficulty label with its corresponding color and raw count, while percentage labels are placed directly on or near each slice. The chart is titled “Distribution of Difficulty,” and visually emphasizes the dominance of Medium and Hard categories, with the remaining categories forming progressively smaller wedges in descending order of size.
